key_bets: Full HTS coil set (TF + PF + CS in REBCO) operates reliably at 25 T peak field under cyclic EM loading, including novel HTS CS coils performing plasma initiation duty cycles
Scaling from Jingtian test magnet's demonstrated 21.7 T to HH170's 25 T target is achievable despite rapid REBCO Jc falloff above 20 T at 20 K and proportionally higher Lorentz forces
AI-based plasma control enabling HH70's 1,337-second steady-state plasma will translate to burning-plasma conditions, reducing disruption frequency and sustaining high capacity factor
Compact high-field geometry (~14 T on-axis, ~70% SPARC volume) achieves Q > 10 at commercial scale, enabling the 'world's smallest and lowest-cost tokamak' value proposition
Tritium breeding blanket can be developed post-2030 (potentially leveraging CFETR WCCB/HCCB/LiPb programs) to achieve TBR > 1 for HH380 despite no disclosed design
ICRH scales from HH70's experimental levels to tens-of-MW burning-plasma operation with adequate wall-plug efficiency (~60–70%) and antenna survivability under D-T neutron flux
China-domestic supply chain (>95% localization via Shanghai Superconductor) scales from prototype to commercial REBCO tape volumes (thousands of km per plant) without significant cost increase
eliminated_costs: Mixed LTS/HTS cryogenic infrastructure — uniform 20 K operation across all coils eliminates need to maintain separate LTS cryogenic circuits at lower temperatures
Large-machine structural material and building volume — compact geometry (~70% SPARC volume vs. ITER's R=6.2 m) reduces site, structures (C210), and absolute capital cost at equivalent Q
International supply chain logistics and export control friction — >95% domestic Chinese sourcing bypasses geopolitical supply risks for China-domestic deployment
Spherical tokamak center-stack constraints — D-shaped conventional aspect ratio permits inboard blanket and near-4π breeding coverage, avoiding outboard-only breeding limitation
novel_costs: Incremental REBCO tape for PF + CS coils beyond TF-only HTS baseline — hts_full_coil_premium ×1.1–×1.3 multiplier on C220103 magnet system account
Full-HTS CS coil reconditioning or replacement under cyclic EM loading at 25 T — accrues to CAS70 O&M in reliability-failure scenarios with no published fatigue data to bound
Quench detection and energy extraction system engineered for a 26+-coil full-HTS system in a neutron environment — no commercial-scale precedent exists
AI-based plasma control system with radiation hardening and redundancy for HH380-scale burning-plasma operation — unvalidated at commercial duty cycle
High-field-specific REBCO tape procurement at 25 T / 20 K performance grade — higher per-km cost than lower-field HTS tape, at commercial plant volumes

risks.description: No commercial design point exists for HH380 (net electric, fusion power, Q, major radius all undisclosed) — LCOE model has no anchor and requires wholesale CFS ARC/SPARC analogue assumptions carrying ±50% capital cost uncertainty
Tritium breeding blanket entirely undisclosed (TRL 1–2) — no concept, material, or TBR target stated; structurally unresolvable until HH380 engineering post-2030
Full HTS CS coils at 25 T under cyclic EM loading have no published fatigue or reliability data — CS reliability failure scenario drops availability to 65% and raises LCOE ~14–22%
Gap from demonstrated 21.7 T (Jingtian) to 25 T (HH170 target) is non-trivial — REBCO Jc falls rapidly above 20 T at 20 K and mechanical loads scale proportionally with field
Power conversion cycle type and thermal efficiency not specified for HH380 — no tritium-compatible heat exchanger or BOP design disclosed
AI plasma control unvalidated at burning-plasma conditions (high neutron flux, sensor degradation, D-T disruption precursors) — underperformance scenario raises LCOE ~9–14%
ICRH scaling from HH70 experimental levels to tens-of-MW burning-plasma operation has undisclosed power, antenna geometry, and first-wall neutron survivability

Chinese regulatory framework for fusion power plants is still being formulated; international harmonization (e.g., proposed Global Organisation for Fusion Energy) may determine HH380 grid-connection and export viability
REBCO tape global production capacity (few thousand km/year) is below fleet-scale demand; tape cost must fall from ~$30–100/kA-m to ~$10/kA-m for commercial competitiveness

Tritium startup inventory (~1 kg at >$35,000/g) and declining CANDU-derived global supply (~25–30 kg, −5.5%/yr) constrain first-of-kind D-T burn; China's indigenous tritium production capability not publicly documented
>95% China-domestic supply chain creates opaque cost basis for international benchmarking and concentrates geopolitical supply risk
First wall / divertor lifetime and remote maintenance scheme not disclosed — dependent on undisclosed wall loading from unknown fusion power
